To prove that a step function is Riemann Integrable, we need to show that the upper and lower Riemann sums converge to the same value as the partition of the interval [a, b] is refined.

Let f be a step function and let P be a partition of [a, b]. Let U(P) and L(P) be the upper and lower Riemann sums, respectively.

For any partition P, we can write:

U(P) = ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i \Delta x_i
L(P) = ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i \Delta x_i

where \Delta x_i is the length of the interval I_i.

Since f is a step function, we can write:

f(x) = ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i \chi_{I_i}(x)

For any x in [a, b], we can find an interval I_j such that x ∈ I_j. Then, we have:

f(x) = c_j

Since c_j is a constant, we have:

f(x) ≤ c_j

and

f(x) ≥ c_j

Therefore, we have:

U(P) ≥ ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i \Delta x_i
L(P) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i \Delta x_i

∑_{i=1}^{n} \Delta x_i = b - a

Therefore, we have:

L(P) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^{n} c_i (b - a)

Since the upper and lower Riemann sums are bounded above and below by the same value, we have:

lim_{P→∞} U(P) = lim_{P→∞} L(P)

Therefore, we have:

lim_{P→∞} U(P) = lim_{P→∞} L(P) = ∫_a^b f(x) dx

Hence, we have proven that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable.

Note that this proof assumes that the step function f is bounded, i.e., there exists a constant M such that |f(x)| ≤ M for all x in [a, b]. If f is not bounded, then the proof does not apply.
